prompt: How do decompilation projects run automated source-variant search at scale for Metrowerks mwcc (GameCube/Wii): decomp-permuter's mwcc support and its known limits, PERM macros, randomization passes that actually change mwcc output, scoring functions and why a permuter score of 0 can still differ from byte identity, parallel/distributed runs, and any other tool (decomp.me scratch automation, AI-assisted search, symbolic rewriting) with published success rates on functions that already compile but do not match? For every claim give the primary source (repo file, issue, PR, compiler manual) and state it as a falsifiable prediction: 'with X, mwcc emits Y; with X', it emits Y''. Mark anything unverified.

query: What measured match rates do decompilation projects report when they run automated source-variant search on GameCube and Wii functions that already compile close to the original but do not match, and who measured them?

Why does a source-level random mutation change the machine code that the Metrowerks compiler emits for some constructs (register allocation order, instruction scheduling, stack slot layout, loop shape) and leave it unchanged for others, and why can a permuter score of zero still fail to be byte-identical?

Why does a small change in how a C function is written cause the Metrowerks PowerPC compiler to assign registers or lay out stack slots differently, even when the resulting instruction sequence looks the same?

What happens when a decompiled function scores as a perfect match by instruction, relocation and symbol comparison but the final linked bytes still differ from the original binary, and how often has this been reported?

At what point does automated permutation of a function stop producing improvements when mwcc is the compiler, and what does the failure look like (unsupported syntax, compiler version or flag mismatch, wrong inlining or section ordering, runs that plateau at a nonzero score)?

Do approaches that rewrite code symbolically or use language models to search for matching source work on mwcc in the same way they work for other compilers and platforms, and what has been reported when they were applied to older console toolchains with different optimizer behavior?

What match rates have GameCube and Wii decompilation projects actually reported when they used language models or automated permutation tools on functions compiled with the Metrowerks compiler, and who measured them?

Why do register allocation, instruction scheduling and inlining decisions in the Metrowerks compiler make some functions nearly impossible to match by rewriting source, and how does this differ from GCC-era compilers?

learning: [DERIVED][MEDIUM] The tool keeps a regression list of matched functions and, in check mode, fails the build when any listed function stops matching or when library code is wrongly counted as decompiled. This turns matching progress into a ratchet that can run in continuous integration, rather than a number someone re-measures by hand. — Capacidad: You can lock in gains by gating every build on a committed list of already-matched functions, so a regression is caught the moment it happens rather than discovered at final link. — Evidencia: The README describes the matched-list workflow, the REGRESSION status, and exit code 1 on regression, but gives no data on how often regressions occur. — Ledger: C11 (S10)

[DERIVED][MEDIUM] In the benchmark, nearly half of AI-phase matches came on the first attempt, and a function unmatched by attempt 3 had only about a one-quarter chance of eventually matching. The permuter mattered most on the IDO-compiled N64 game (matching 3-4 functions per run) and matched none on the ARM/GBA game, so permutation value depends on how well the tool supports the compiler. Metrowerks support was not measured in these sources. — Capacidad: You can decide how much attempt budget and permutation tooling to fund per function, and stop spending on functions that have not matched early. — Evidencia: Benchmark figures: roughly half of matches on first AI attempt, about 25% conditional match chance after attempt 3, permuter matches 3-4 per run on Animal Forest and none on Sonic Advance 3. — Ledger: C15 (S18)
